senses.definition: Set up so that one side works against the other.
senses.caution: About a person or a team it can sound hostile. About tests or models it is neutral and means built to find weaknesses.
senses.example: We ran an adversarial review, where one engineer's only job was to find holes in the plan.

cues.text: You want a red-team style test where one group's only goal is to find the inputs that make your model fail. What adjective describes that kind of testing?
Two models are trained against each other, one making fakes and the other trying to catch them. You name the kind of setup in the paper.
A courtroom system pits two sides against each other so the truth comes out of the clash. What adjective names that kind of system?

distractors: Known to only a few people with special training in the subject.
Easy to use again, because running it a second time changes nothing.
Present in scattered places rather than everywhere at once.
